Class Udp

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.net.Udp
public final class Udp extends Object
Allocation-free UDP transport recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.

One socket is available to a Juno program. Call listen(int) once after Wi-Fi is connected, then use broadcast(int, byte[], int) as the discovery primitive, send(int[], int, byte[], int) to produce a datagram for a known peer, and receive(byte[], int, int[]) to consume the next datagram without blocking. The same API is lowered to WiFiUDP on UNO R4 WiFi and BridgeUDP on UNO Q.

An endpoint is a caller-owned int[5] containing the four IPv4 octets followed by the UDP port. Payloads are caller-owned byte arrays; the runtime never allocates or retains them. UDP is unreliable and unordered, so applications that require delivery must add sequence numbers, acknowledgements, or retries to their protocol.

  • Method Details

    • listen

      public static boolean listen(int localPort)
      Binds the program's UDP socket to localPort. Calling this again closes the previous socket first. Returns true when the socket was opened.

    • send

      public static int send(int[] address, int remotePort, byte[] payload, int length)
      Sends length bytes from payload to the IPv4 address and remotePort. address must contain at least four octets. Returns the payload length on success or -1 when the socket is not listening or the packet could not be sent.

    • broadcast

      public static int broadcast(int remotePort, byte[] payload, int length)
      Sends length bytes to the link-local IPv4 all-hosts group at remotePort. This portable group broadcast is the minimum building block for LAN discovery and remains within the local network. Returns the payload length on success or -1 on failure.

    • receive

      public static int receive(byte[] payload, int capacity, int[] source)
      Non-blockingly consumes the next datagram. At most capacity bytes are copied into payload; excess bytes in that datagram are discarded. capacity must be positive. On success, source receives the sender's four IPv4 octets and port. Returns the copied byte count, 0 when no packet is waiting, or -1 for invalid state/input (including non-positive capacity) or a read failure.

    • stop

      public static void stop()
      Closes the socket.
